title: Combine a server-rendered dashboard with live client updates
businessContext: A dashboard remounts the full application every few seconds to fetch a new session and replace all data.
problemStatement: Design the system for 5,000 connected users; events can be duplicated and delivered out of order. Produce the component/data-flow diagram, request and mutation contracts, cache/trust boundaries, capacity assumptions, failure recovery and rollout gates. State which decisions change between Next.js 15 and 16 instead of using a framework API as a substitute for an architectural guarantee.
constraints: Reconcile live events without cross-account leakage.
candidateTasks: Draw components and annotate ownership of data, identity, caches and durable work.
Specify contracts/schema and quantify the capacity/freshness assumptions.
Walk through the failure scenario and design measurable acceptance tests.
Compare the reference decisions and answer the changed-requirement interview prompt.

systemDesignReqs.scale: 5,000 connected users; events can be duplicated and delivered out of order
functional: Reconcile live events without cross-account leakage.
nonFunctional: State an explicit latency, freshness and recovery budget rather than inventing guarantees.
Keep actor/tenant isolation and failure ownership observable.
assumptions: A patched App Router deployment; platform-specific infrastructure support must be verified.
Next.js version and Cache Components configuration are explicit design inputs.

hints: Fetch an authorized versioned initial snapshot on the server and hydrate a small client island for live state.

A stale connection can deliver events after the user switches tenants. Reject messages by active subscription ownership and server-authorized channel scope; client-side filtering alone cannot secure the upstream stream.
alternativeApproaches: Use it deliberately for server-owned reconciliation rather than as an unbounded per-event rebuild. Coalesce refreshes, preserve client state and measure server load; some events can update an admitted client projection directly.
commonMistakes: Claiming a cache API provides transactions, durable delivery or cross-region consistency.
Omitting authorization, recovery budgets or evidence from an otherwise attractive component diagram.

verification: Duplicate/reorder events and introduce sequence gaps.
Disconnect, reconnect and change accounts during catch-up.
Measure visible freshness, subscription cleanup and bounded memory growth.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
